45498-history-of-the-union-jack-and-flag.title: to other National Ensigns
45498-history-of-the-union-jack-and-flag.creator: Barlow Cumberland, M.A.
45498-history-of-the-union-jack-and-flag.description: A book by Barlow Cumberland, M.A.. The chapters on the history of the Jacks in the Thirteen American Colonies and in the United States are also new ground and may be of novel interest to not a few. The added information on the proper proportions of our Union Jack, and the directions and reasons for the proper making of its parts, may serve to correct some of the unhappy errors which now exist and may interest all in the observation and study of flags.

arxiv-2105-08774.title: Security of continuous-variable quantum key distribution against canonical attacks Thanks: This work was funded by the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation program under grant agreement No 820466 (CiViQ: “Continuous Variable Quantum Communications”).
arxiv-2105-08774.creator: Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola
arxiv-2105-08774.description: Abstract We investigate the performance of Gaussian-modulated coherent-state QKD protocols in the presence of canonical attacks, which are collective Gaussian attacks resulting in Gaussian channels described by one of the possible canonical forms. We present asymptotic key rates and then we extend the results to the finite-size regime using a recently-developed toolbox for composable security.

arxiv-2105-13833.title: Umbilical submanifolds of ℍ k × 𝕊 n − k + 1 \mathbb{H}^{k}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-k+1} .
arxiv-2105-13833.description: Abstract . In this article we complete the classification of the umbilical submanifolds of a Riemannian product of space forms, addressing the case of a conformally flat product ℍ k × 𝕊 n − k + 1 \mathbb{H}^{k}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-k+1} , which has not been covered in previous works on the subject.

arxiv-2206-07339.title: Efficient variable cell shape geometry optimization Journal: Journal of Computational Physics: X
arxiv-2206-07339.creator: Moritz Gubler, Marco Krummenacher, Hannes Huber, Stefan Goedecker
arxiv-2206-07339.description: Abstract A fast and reliable geometry optimization algorithm is presented that optimizes atomic positions and lattice vectors simultaneously. Using a series of benchmarks, it is shown that the method presented in this paper outperforms in most cases the standard optimization methods implemented in popular codes such as Quantum ESPRESSO and VASP.

arxiv-2209-10017.title: Compress-Forward Schemes for General Networks This material is based upon work partially supported by NSF Contract CNS-1302182, AFOSR Contract FA9550-13-1-0008, and NSF Science & Technology Center Grant CCF-0939370.
arxiv-2209-10017.creator: Jonathan Ponniah
arxiv-2209-10017.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Ponniah. Compress-forward (CF) schemes are studied in general networks. The CF rate for the one-relay channel defines outerbounds on both the CF rate for general networks and the compression rate-vector region supporting this rate. We show the outerbound is achievable using regular decoding with constant encoding delays, avoiding the exponential delays and restrictions on bidirectional communication in noisy network coding and backward decoding.

arxiv-2209-11285.title: Bézier interpolation improves the inference of dynamical models from data
arxiv-2209-11285.creator: Kai Shimagaki, John P. Barton
arxiv-2209-11285.description: Abstract Many dynamical systems, from quantum many-body systems to evolving populations to financial markets, are described by stochastic processes. Parameters characterizing such processes can often be inferred using information integrated over stochastic paths. However, estimating time-integrated quantities from real data with limited time resolution is challenging. Here, we propose a framework for accurately estimating time-integrated quantities using Bézier interpolation.

arxiv-2212-04218.title: Structural Reductions and Stutter Sensitive Properties
arxiv-2212-04218.creator: Emmanuel Paviot-Adet, Denis Poitrenaud ORCID:0000-0001-9013-4413, Etienne Renault ORCID:0000-0001-9013-4413, Yann Thierry-Mieg ORCID:0000-0001-7775-1978
arxiv-2212-04218.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emmanuel Paviot-Adet, Denis Poitrenaud ORCID:0000-0001-9013-4413, Etienne Renault ORCID:0000-0001-9013-4413, Yann Thierry-Mieg ORCID:0000-0001-7775-1978. Verification of properties expressed as ω \omega -regular languages such as LTL can benefit hugely from stutter insensitivity, using a diverse set of reduction strategies. However properties that are not stutter invariant, for instance due to the use of the neXt operator of LTL or to some form of counting in the logic, are not covered by these techniques in general.

arxiv-2306-12112.title: Partial Schauder estimates for unbounded solutions of the Kolmogorov equation
arxiv-2306-12112.creator: Andrzej Palczewski
arxiv-2306-12112.description: Abstract The goal of the paper is to show, under possibly weak assumptions, that the function given by the Feynman-Kac formula is a classical solution of the associated Kolmogorov equation. We also show that although this solution is unbounded it fulfills Schauder’s estimates.

arxiv-2310-00514.title: The CSP Dichotomy, the Axiom of Choice, and Cyclic Polymorphisms Thanks: The first and third authors were supported by Hungarian Academy of Sciences Momentum Grant no. 2022-58 and National Research, Development and Innovation Office ( NKFIH) grants no. 113047, 129211. The second author was supported
arxiv-2310-00514.creator: Tamás Kátay, László Márton Tóth, Zoltán Vidnyánszky
arxiv-2310-00514.description: Abstract . We study Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) with infinite instances and finite templates. We show that the dichotomy between easy and hard problems – established by Bulatov and Zhuk in the finite case – presents itself as the strength of the corresponding De Bruijn-Erdős-type compactness theorem over ZF.

arxiv-2404-02211.creator: K. E. Heintz, G. B. Brammer, D. Watson, P. A. Oesch, L. C. Keating, M. J. Hayes, Abdurro’uf, K. Z. Arellano-Córdova, A. C. Carnall, C. R. Christiansen, F. Cullen, R. arxiv-2404-02211.description: Abstract Context. One of the surprising early findings with JWST has been the discovery of a strong “roll-over” or a softening of the absorption edge of Ly α \alpha in a large number of galaxies at z ≳ 6 z\gtrsim 6 , in addition to systematic offsets from photometric redshift estimates and fundamental galaxy scaling relations.

arxiv-2405-00717.title: Exploring News Summarization and Enrichment in a Highly Resource-Scarce Indian Language: A Case Study of Mizo
arxiv-2405-00717.description: Abstract Obtaining sufficient information in one’s mother tongue is crucial for satisfying the information needs of the users. While high-resource languages have abundant online resources, the situation is less than ideal for very low-resource languages. Moreover, the insufficient reporting of vital national and international events continues to be a worry, especially in languages with scarce resources, like Mizo .

arxiv-2405-07385.title: All-multiplicity amplitudes in impulsive PP-waves from the worldline formalism
arxiv-2405-07385.creator: and Karthik Rajeev
arxiv-2405-07385.description: Abstract We use the worldline formalism to derive Bern-Kosower type Master Formulae for the tree-level scattering of a charged particle and an arbitrary number of photons on impulsive PP-waves, where the coupling of the PP-wave to matter is treated fully non-perturbatively.

arxiv-2504-09794.description: Abstract . We show that every sufficiently large oriented graph G G with minimum indegree and outdegree both at least ( 3 ​ | V ⁡ ( G ) | − 1 ) / 8 (3|V(G)|-1)/8 contains every orientation of a Hamilton cycle.

arxiv-2507-00699.title: A Hierarchical and Evolvable Benchmark for Fine-Grained Code Instruction Following with Multi-Turn Feedback * Corresponding author.
arxiv-2507-00699.creator: Guoliang Duan 1 , Mingwei Liu 1 * , Yanlin Wang 1 , Chong Wang 2 , Xin Peng 3 , Zibin Zheng 1
arxiv-2507-00699.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have advanced significantly in code generation, yet their ability to follow complex programming instructions with layered and diverse constraints remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks often prioritize functional correctness, overlooking the nuanced requirements found in real-world development.

arxiv-2512-23126.title: InSPO: Unlocking Intrinsic Self-Reflection for LLM Preference Optimization
arxiv-2512-23126.creator: Yu Li, Tian Lan, Zhengling Qi
arxiv-2512-23126.description: Abstract Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and its variants have become the standard for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) due to their simplicity and offline stability. However, we identify two fundamental limitations that undermine the reliability and optimality of DPO and its equivalents.

europmc-pmc2292207.title: A comparison of two methods for estimating prevalence ratios.
europmc-pmc2292207.creator: Petersen MR, Deddens JA.
europmc-pmc2292207.description: Background It is usually preferable to model and estimate prevalence ratios instead of odds ratios in cross-sectional studies when diseases or injuries are not rare. Problems with existing methods of modeling prevalence ratios include lack of convergence, overestimated standard

plos-pone-0348506.creator: Yuanxiang Peng
plos-pone-0348506.description: Sustainability-induced loyalty in festival tourism: Examining the mediating pathways between sustainable practices and visitor behavioral support

pmc-10712062.title: Y chromosome AZFc microdeletion may have negative effect on embryo euploidy: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-10712062.creator: Wei Jiang, Qijun Xie, Xin Li, Ye Yang, Ting Luan, Danyu Ni, Yuting Chen, Xinyu Wang, Chun Zhao, Xiufeng Ling
pmc-10712062.description: BackgroundEmbryo aneuploidy is a main of principal reason of pregnancy loss, in vitro fertilization (IVF) failure and birth defects in offspring. Previous researchs have demonstrated that Y chromosome AZFc microdeletion was associated with reproduction outcomes, however, the relationship between Y chromosome AZFc microdeletion and embryo aneuploidy remains unexplored.

pmc-11603839.title: A novel pan-epitope based nanovaccine self-assembled with CpG enhances immune responses against flavivirus
pmc-11603839.creator: Jiuxiang He, Xiaoyan Ding, Jing Zhao, Jie Zeng, Yuxin Zhou, Wen Xiao, Dong Hua, Minchi Liu, Hongxia Guo, Yu Zhang, Minyue Qiu, Jintao Li
pmc-11603839.description: BackgroundFlavivirus is a highly prevalent and outbreak-prone disease, affecting billions of individuals annually and posing substantial public health challenges. Vaccination is critical to reducing the global impact of flavivirus infections, making the development of a safe and effective vaccine a top priority.

pmc-11672479.title: Machine Learning-Assisted SERS Reveals the Biochemical Signature of Enhanced Protein Secretion from Surface-Modified Magnetic Nanoparticles
pmc-11672479.creator: Ibrahim Dagci, Kubra Solak, Nazli Oncer, Seyda Yildiz Arslan, Yagmur Unver, Mehmet Yilmaz, Ahmet Mavi
pmc-11672479.description: This study introduces a novel investigation of the interaction between Komagataella phaffii cells and iron oxide-based magnetic nanoparticles (Fe3O4 MNPs) via protein secretion and machine learning (ML)-assisted surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). For the first time, we produced Fe3O4, Fe3O4@PEG, Fe3O4@PEI10kDa, and Fe3O4@PEI25kDa MNPs by a one-pot coprecipitation reaction.

pmc-12365004.title: Evaluation of Global Surgery Perspectives and Knowledge Amongst Past Surgical Trainees in East, Central, and Southern Africa: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-12365004.creator: Yvan Zolo, Wakisa Mulwafu, Salome Maswime
pmc-12365004.description: Background and AimsAfrica faces a shortage of academic Global Surgery programs, limiting trainee exposure despite pressing surgical care inequities. Global Surgery seeks to improve access through systems and policy strengthening.MethodsA cross‐sectional electronic survey was conducted among COSECSA‐affiliated registrars and specialists to assess their Global Surgery knowledge and perspectives.

pmc-12468437.title: Deep Learning for Heart Sound Abnormality of Infants: Proof-of-Concept Study of 1D and 2D Representations †
pmc-12468437.creator: Eashita Wazed, Jimin Lee, Hieyong Jeong
pmc-12468437.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highlights What are the main findings? This study proposes a novel multimodal deep learning framework that uniquely integrates both 1D time-series and 2D image representations of infant heart sounds, achieving a state-of-the-art accuracy of 98.91% for abnormality detection.The study systematically demonstrates that this fusion model not only improves classification performance over using either data representation alone but also significantly reduces the computational training cost compared to purely image-based models. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-12470278.title: Investigating the Metabolic Benefits of Magnetic Mitohormesis in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
pmc-12470278.creator: Fan Shuen Tseng, Gek Hsiang Lim, Yong Mong Bee, Phong Ching Lee, Yee Kit Tai, Alfredo Franco-Obregón, Hong Chang Tan, Alfredo Caturano
pmc-12470278.description: Background/Objectives: Exercise is a key pillar in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but adherence rates to physical activity are poor. Pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) therapy, termed magnetic mitohormesis (MM), has been shown in preclinical and early human studies to mimic the metabolic benefits of exercise without physical strain. However, its effects on glycemic control remain unknown.

pmc-12609672.title: Seaweed Foliar Biostimulants Improve Growth and Phytochemicals of Thai Basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) in a Plant Factory
pmc-12609672.creator: Vu Phong Lam, Gwonjeong Bok, Dao Nhan Loi, Manh Cuong Do, Jongseok Park, Mason MacDonald, Lord Abbey, Raphael Ofoe
pmc-12609672.description: This study aimed to identify the optimal concentration of seaweed extract (SE) for enhancing growth, photosynthetic traits, antioxidant activity, and bioactive compound accumulation in Thai basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) plants cultivated in a fully controlled plant factory. Basil plants were foliar-sprayed twice weekly with five SE concentrations (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 mL·L−1), while untreated plants served as controls.

pmc-12997212.title: Progression patterns and clinical outcomes in patients with cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma following anti-PD-1 therapy failure
pmc-12997212.creator: K Khaddour, P Kote, M Liu, A Giobbie-Hurder, I Dryg, A Goyal, JP Guenette, JD Schoenfeld, DN Margalit, RB Tishler, EM Rettig, RKV Sethi, DJ Annino, LA Goguen, R Uppaluri, C Yoon, M de Simone, NA Ran, J Stevens, AH Waldman, ES Ruiz, JV Cohen, AW Silk, GJ Hanna
pmc-12997212.description: BackgroundAnti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) therapy is the cornerstone for managing advanced cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma (CSCC). Nevertheless, many patients experience treatment failure. Limited data exist regarding outcomes following anti-PD-1 failure. This study investigates progression patterns and clinical outcomes in CSCC patients post-anti-PD-1 therapy.

pmc-13413643.title: Genomic and Functional Characterization of the Endophytic Bacillus siamensis Strain BACIII with Plant Growth-Promoting and Antifungal Activity
pmc-13413643.creator: Jefferson Brendon Almeida dos Reis, Sofia Coradini Schirmer, Maria Regina Silveira Sartori da Silva, Andrei Stecca Steindorff, Patrícia Cardoso Cortelo, Georgios Joannis Pappas, Helson Mario Martins do Vale
pmc-13413643.description: Endophytic bacteria of the Bacillus subtilis species complex are known for plant growth promotion and antifungal activity, although strain-specific traits remain poorly understood. This study characterized the Bacillus siamensis strain BACIII, isolated from asymptomatic soybean roots in a charcoal rot-affected area, using whole-genome analysis and phenotypic assays.

pmc-13624661.title: CUT&ID for simultaneous profiling of protein–DNA and protein–protein interactions
pmc-13624661.creator: Anna Nordin, Claudio Cantù
pmc-13624661.description: We developed CUT&ID to simultaneously profile the native genomics and proteomics associations of any endogenous target, in a single workflow with no need for transgenesis. CUT&ID is enabled by a fusion protein of TurboID, protein A/G, and micrococcal nuclease, which drives sequential target recognition, proximal protein biotinylation, and DNA cleavage in living cells.
